name: Standard Scramble

waypoints.name: Slate Pass Trailhead
waypoints.note: Second switchback on the Slate Peak spur above Harts Pass, below the road's gated end; the Slate Pass Trail drops from here to the Robinson Creek (Middle Fork Pasayten) Trail #478 in the Pasayten Wilderness.

waypoints.name: Berk Creek Trail junction
waypoints.note: Low point of the Robinson Creek/Middle Fork Pasayten valley where the Berk Creek Trail forks north toward Freds Lake and Freds Pass; expect heavy blowdown on this stretch even by Pasayten standards.

waypoints.name: Freds Pass
waypoints.note: 7,100-ft pass gained via the Berk Creek Trail, dividing the Berk Creek and Eureka Creek drainages — the key navigation point of the cross-country approach.
waypoints.directions: Turn onto the Eureka Creek Trail and climb east along Berk Creek to Freds Lake, the last reliable water and a common camp, then continue up the fading tread to Freds Pass at about 7,100 ft.

waypoints.name: Shellrock Pass bench
waypoints.note: Roughly half-acre bench just southwest of 7,487-ft Shellrock Pass, the standard staging camp used for Ptarmigan and the other Pasayten Eleven summits.
waypoints.directions: Drop east from the pass into the head of the Eureka Creek basin and cross it eastward on faint tread that is often lost in blowdown, so cairns and map work are needed; the creek crossing can be difficult in snowmelt. Climb to the broad bench just southwest of Shellrock Pass at about 7,500 ft.

waypoints.name: 7,800-ft tarn, Ptarmigan south slopes
waypoints.note: Small tarn reported reliable into late season — the last dependable water before the final summit push.

waypoints.name: South ridge gain point
waypoints.note: Leave the tarn basin and scramble cross-country over talus onto the crest of Ptarmigan's south ridge.

waypoints.name: Ptarmigan Peak
waypoints.note: True summit (8,614 ft per recent lidar survey); Class 2-3 talus and short rock steps for the final stretch, with views across the remote Pasayten Eleven.

approach: There is no short trailhead-to-base approach for Ptarmigan Peak — it's a deep-interior Pasayten summit reached on a multi-day backpack, and the standard approach is the same trail system used to stage a high camp near Shellrock Pass. From the Slate Pass trailhead (~6,900 ft, reached via the Hart's Pass Road/FR-5400 past the Hart's Pass Guard Station), start on the Slate Pass Trail (#498), which drops steeply through larch stands and avalanche-lily meadows for a few miles, losing roughly 1,500 ft, to its junction with the Middle Fork Pasayten River Trail / Robinson Creek Trail (#478) at around 5,300–5,400 ft. Turn north (right) on Trail #478 and follow the Middle Fork Pasayten valley downstream, fording several tributary creeks (can run high and be a real obstacle in early-season/high-runoff conditions) and passing the side junction to Tatoosh Buttes (Trail #485) around the 8–9 mile mark; this stretch has a long-standing reputation for heavy blowdown (parties describe a thousand or so downed logs), so expect slow, log-hopping travel. Continue north to the Berk Creek junction, then climb east on the Freds Pass trail, passing Freds Lake (reliable water and a common overnight stop) around mile 14–15, over Freds Pass, and across the head of the Eureka Creek basin — parties note the tread here is faint or completely obscured by blowdown near the Eureka Creek turn, so cairns and map/GPS work are needed — to Shellrock Pass around mile 17–18 (roughly 7,400–7,500 ft). A broad half-acre bench just southwest of Shellrock Pass is the standard high camp and staging area for Ptarmigan and neighboring peaks (Lago, Carru, Osceola). From camp it's off-trail: gain the ridge crest north of camp and follow open alpine tundra and talus across the shoulder of Mount Lago (via the Lago–Carru col on some variations) to Ptarmigan's south ridge — roughly 2–3 more cross-country miles and 1,000–1,200 ft of gain, mostly class 2 over tundra and talus with some loose rock on the ridge crest. A shorter, less-traveled alternative approaches from the east via the end of Eightmile Creek Road and the Eightmile Pass–Hidden Lake Trail (~15 miles) to Ptarmigan Creek, then 2–3 miles cross-country through brush to the base — shorter on paper but rougher, brushier, and far less maintained than the Slate Pass line, which is the de facto standard.
descent_text: This is a walk-off/scramble descent with no rappelling anywhere on the route (rappels: 0). From the summit, reverse the south ridge and talus slopes back toward the Shellrock Pass camp bench — parties describe class 3 scrambling on the ridge near Points 8165 and 8207 with one short, avoidable class-4 step, easing to class 2 tundra and talus lower down; some parties vary the line by continuing the ridge traverse over Mount Lago before dropping to the tarn/camp rather than reversing the exact ascent line, but the character (talus/tundra ridge-walking, no technical terrain) is the same either way. From the high camp near Shellrock Pass, the multi-day walk-out simply reverses the approach trail: back across the head of Eureka Creek, over Freds Pass, down Berk Creek to the Middle Fork Pasayten River Trail (#478), south past Tatoosh Buttes, and back up the Slate Pass Trail (#498) to the Slate Pass trailhead (about 1,500 ft of final climbing on tired legs). No ropes, anchors, or rappels are used at any point on the standard route or its variations.
